metadata.title: Optimal Linear Additive Memory in Finite Ordered Structures: Zeckendorf Events and Decidable-Envelope Phase Barriers
metadata.description: We study generated memory required for first-order arithmetic recovery on finite ordered carriers. In a fixed finite bounded-arity base-sorted signature, uniform truncated addition requires Omega(m) added primitive support. A prefix-generated differential Zeckendorf history attains this bound: storing only digit-change events gives |U_m|+|D_m|=2m-2-s_F(m-1)=Theta(m), while the full Zeckendorf incidence relation and truncated addition remain uniformly first-order recoverable. The resulting family is exact AL1: multiplication is excluded by a Decidable Coherent Envelope (DCE) barrier. Differential binary/BIT history also has Theta(m) support but remains AL2, proving that equal linear materialized cost does not determine arithmetic phase. DCE is preserved under coherently liftable fixed-dimensional first-order interpretations, including definable quotients, yielding a non-collapse theorem between the linear Zeckendorf and BIT event families. English and Russian manuscripts and reproducibility scripts are included.
